text:
Maya: quick heads-up — I see a regression on INT8 weight-only (AWQ) p50 after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak. Short-chat workload (seq <= 128) p50 went from ~48ms to ~62ms. Suspect packing alignment + batching heuristic interaction causing extra memcpy / kernel fallbacks.

Lin: can you paste the flame/trace or top hot functions? which kernel is hot?

Maya: pasting perf dump from PerfBot:
```
PERF_SUMMARY
p50: 62ms (was 48ms)
p95: 180ms (stable)
tokens/sec: -8%
hot: pack_unaligned_copy, awq_unpack_fallback_kernel
kv_hit_rate: 0.92 -> 0.85
memcpy spikes @ pack_unaligned: 3.2MB/s
awq_unpack_fallback_rate: 1200/s
batch_size_median: 4 -> 2 (after routing change)
```

PerfBot: Telemetry snapshot 2168002468: kernel_fallback_rate=0.12, pack_unaligned_copies=3.4MB/s spike, median_batch=2, kv_hit_rate=0.85

Jorge: was the routing change the one that biased AWQ kernels for groupsize==64 alignment? If we force alignment to 64 we can mis-align real groups like 16/32 and cause extra per-request packing. We should make the packer group-aware (align to quant group_stride) not to a fixed 64 boundary.

Rachel: also seeing KV cache churn — when packing/layout changes we get more cache misses for short prefixes. The miss pattern matches the memcpy spikes (we regen packed keys). I can share diffs of prepacked key bytes if needed.

Devon: quick config idea to test: set kernel_policy = "prefer_awq_if(groupsize <= 32 && kv_hit_rate >= 0.9)" and turn off forced_alignment. Also try packing_threads=2 to avoid single-threaded serial copies.

Lin: I'll run a structured sweep: groupsize in [8,16,32,64] x batch_size in [1,2,4] with slab-prefetch on/off and collect kernel_fallback, pack_copy, kv_hit_rate. Can someone attach the repro replay?

Maya: repro is short-chat-replay v2 (internal replay id 2026-03-shortchat-01). Repro steps: run \`./replay --workload short-chat --profile --trace memcopy,kernel_fallback\` Linked snapshot: https://internal.redwood/perf/2168. I'll open a triage PR with the perf trace and minimal repro.

Jorge: if AWQ unpack path is falling back, maybe the quant calibration layout differs (AWQ uses per-group bias packing). Compare AWQ vs GPTQ packed bytes for same weights; if layout differs we should emit a packing-compatibility tag so runtime can choose compatible kernel without repack.

PerfBot: PerfBot created ticket PF-3921: "awq-pack-alignment-fallback-regress" assigned eng-ml, severity=medium, link: https://internal.redwood/ops/PF-3921

Rachel: note — GPTQ path didn't show regression, so likely AWQ-specific packing or calibration alignment. I'd add a fast byte-compare between pack outputs to identify where layout diverges.

Devon: I'll prototype a conservative fallback: if awq_unpack_fallback_rate > 5% for a route, route to GPTQ kernel for groupsize > 32, or disable the forced 64-align. That should be quick AB to confirm impact.

Maya: proposed action items: 1) Lin runs sweep and posts CSV, 2) Devon builds AB with kernel_policy tweak + packing_threads change, 3) I open bisect PR for the routing tweak revert and include perf logs. We'll sync tomorrow 10:00 in eng-ml. cc @PerfBot

Lin: sounds good — I'll drop results in this thread and ping when the sweep finishes.

Devon: on it, will try the policy patch and a build targeting dedicated to match real GPU layout.

Maya: thanks all — priority is to get p50 back without degrading p95. If AB confirms, we'll roll the kernel routing tweak back and follow up with a proper packer that aligns to quant group_stride.

PerfBot: Note: automated nightly job will run pack-compatibility checks and emit alerts if pack layout entropy increases by >2% across recent builds.

Rachel: adding one more note — check the calibration step in AWQ CI: a small change in reorder in calibration can change pack padding. I'll hunt that in calibration tests too.

Maya: OK — logging PF-3921, triage PR opened, follow-ups in morning. Thanks.
